title: Lifecycle Hooks
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Lifecycle Hooks in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Lifecycle Hooks within Component Architecture and Lifecycle. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Correct lifecycle placement prevents stale DOM assumptions, duplicated subscriptions, and memory leaks.

content_blocks.title: Lifecycle Hooks: Lifecycle and cleanup
content_blocks.alt_text: Lifecycle and cleanup diagram for lesson 56: Lifecycle Hooks. Create state before relying on the DOM → Use the right hook and nextTick when needed → Remove listeners, timers, and subscriptions
content_blocks.caption: Lifecycle flow: run DOM-dependent work at the correct phase and clean up external effects when the component no longer needs them.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Lifecycle hooks, template refs, update scheduling, and error capture let components coordinate with the DOM and external systems. This lesson focuses on Lifecycle Hooks. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: onBeforeMount() and onMounted()
items.text: For onBeforeMount() and onMounted(), place DOM or external-system work in the lifecycle phase where the needed element exists, then clean up timers, listeners, observers, or subscriptions when the component no longer needs them. Use nextTick() when code must wait for Vue's queued DOM update.

items.title: onBeforeUpdate() and onUpdated()
items.text: For onBeforeUpdate() and onUpdated(), connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: onBeforeUnmount() and onUnmounted()
items.text: For onBeforeUnmount() and onUnmounted(), place DOM or external-system work in the lifecycle phase where the needed element exists, then clean up timers, listeners, observers, or subscriptions when the component no longer needs them. Use nextTick() when code must wait for Vue's queued DOM update.

content_blocks.expected_output: A resize logs the viewport width; when the component unmounts the listener is removed.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run locally and mount/unmount the component. Cleanup is essential when listeners, timers, or subscriptions outlive one render.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Lifecycle Hooks with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “onBeforeUpdate() and onUpdated()”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Lifecycle hooks, template refs, update scheduling, and error capture let components coordinate with the DOM and external systems. For Lifecycle Hooks, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Lifecycle Hooks” that applies “onBeforeMount() and onMounted()”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “onBeforeMount() and onMounted()”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Lifecycle Hooks belongs to the broader area Component Architecture and Lifecycle.
The main concept to practice is onBeforeMount() and onMounted().
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
